case_number: Criminal Appeal No. 658 of 2022 and Criminal Appeal No. 659 of 2022

parties.respondent: Mohammed Bhava & Anr; Mohammed Musthafa & Anr

summary: The appeals challenge the High Court of Karnataka's grant of anticipatory and regular bail to two accused, Mohammed Bhava and Mohammed Musthafa, in a heinous premeditated murder case under IPC sections 143, 147, 148, 302, 307, 395, and 149. The appellant, son of the deceased, argued that the High Court mechanically granted bail without considering gravity, witness testimony, and threat to witnesses. The respondents claimed lack of involvement and reliance on bail jurisprudence favoring liberty. The Supreme Court examined whether bail was granted without proper application of mind and noted that bail can be cancelled not only for supervening circumstances but also if relevant material or gravity of offence was ignored. Precedents on bail discretion and cancellation were analyzed.
legal_provisions_cited: Ram Govind Upadhyay Vs. Sudarshan Singh and Others (2002) 3 SCC 598
Arnab Manoranjan Goswami Vs. State of Maharashtra & Ors. (2021) 2 SCC 427
Daulat Ram and Others v. State of Haryana (1995) 1 SCC 349
State (Delhi Admn) v. Sanjay Gandhi (1978) 2 SCC 411
Kashmira Singh v. Duman Singh (1996) 4 SCC 693
X v. State of Telangana (2020) 16 SCC 511
Vipan Kumar Dhir Vs. State of Punjab and Anr. 2021 SCC OnLine SC 854
final_judgment: The Court remanded the matter to the High Court for reconsideration of bail orders with proper application of mind, taking into account the gravity of the offence, material on record, and threat to witnesses, in light of the principles discussed.
